summary:
Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, HELM is an offline-first, interactive medical decision support system designed for long-duration spaceflight. The platform empowers astronauts to manage their own well-being during critical communication delays with Earth. The architecture seamlessly integrates a Python FastAPI backend and a local SQLite database with a responsive HTML/JS dashboard, ensuring zero-latency, local data processing in isolated environments.

HELM aggregates a comprehensive suite of mission data across five health domains: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, radiation, nutrition, and psychological. It tracks real-time vitals like SpO2, blood pressure, and mood, alongside cabin environment metrics such as oxygen partial pressure and CO2 levels. To prevent alert fatigue caused by normal microgravity adaptation, HELM’s dynamic scoring engine evaluates vitals against strict NASA-anchored thresholds and a customized 20% physiological drift baseline.

Beyond data logging, the system integrates a MediaPipe-powered computer vision module for physical mobility assessments and an LLM-driven AI Health Assistant that provides immediate, localized triage protocols. By combining robust data pipelines, autonomous wellness calculations, and agentic AI diagnostics into a cohesive local network, HELM ensures crews maintain peak operational readiness and safety in deep space.
details:
What It Does and How It Works

HELM is an offline-first, autonomous medical decision support system designed specifically for long-duration spaceflight. The system functions as a localized mission control for crew health, operating entirely independently of Earth-based servers.

It works by aggregating daily input from astronauts across five core health domains: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, radiation & immune, nutrition & metabolic, and psychological. The frontend dashboard captures critical vitals (such as SpO2, blood pressure, body temperature, mood, and fatigue) alongside cabin environment metrics (like O2 partial pressure and CO2 levels). This data is securely pushed to a localized backend API, where a dynamic scoring engine processes it against strict NASA-anchored thresholds. Furthermore, HELM integrates an AI Health Assistant for immediate triage protocols and utilizes a computer vision module to conduct physical mobility and musculoskeletal assessments.

Project Benefits

  • Zero-Latency Decision Support: By processing all data locally, HELM completely circumvents the communication delays associated with deep space travel, giving astronauts instantaneous medical feedback.
  • Reduction of Alert Fatigue: Instead of strictly comparing astronaut vitals to Earth-bound norms, the scoring engine calculates a 20% physiological drift against the crew member's personal baseline, reducing false alarms caused by normal microgravity adaptation.
  • Holistic Health Tracking: It prevents "masking" by ensuring that critical deterioration in one isolated system (e.g., a radiation spike) appropriately impacts the overall wellness and autonomy scores, even if other metrics like sleep and nutrition remain nominal.

Intended Impact

The primary impact of HELM is crew autonomy. As missions push further to the Moon and Mars, the standard 20-minute one-way signal delay makes real-time medical guidance from Earth impossible. HELM empowers astronauts to monitor their own health trends, execute localized triage, and maintain peak operational readiness, ultimately ensuring mission safety and success in highly isolated environments.

Tools, Languages, and Software

  • Backend & Logic: Python, FastAPI, and Uvicorn were used to build a robust, lightweight local server capable of handling API requests without internet access.
  • Database: SQLite was utilized for the local helm_offline.db database, ensuring persistent, structured data storage for long-term mission analytics directly on the device.
  • Frontend: A responsive, modular dashboard built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript, served seamlessly from the local network environment.
  • Computer Vision: OpenCV and Google MediaPipe were integrated to track physical mobility indexes and structural health through live camera feeds.
  • AI & LLM Integration: LangChain and local agentic AI pipelines were employed to power the interactive health assistant.
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub were used for multi-branch repository management, facilitating the successful integration of Logic, Frontend, Vision, and LLM branches.

CREATIVITY

HELM's creativity lies in its intersection of deterministic medical logic and autonomous AI. Rather than building a static data logger, the project incorporates a computer vision mobility scanner that translates physical movements into quantifiable database metrics.

Additionally, the algorithmic approach to the Wellness Score is highly creative: it dynamically converts unit inputs (like kPa to mmHg) on the fly and utilizes a personalized baseline drift calculation, marrying clinical deterioration tracking with the unique realities of space medicine.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY THE TEAM

  • The Physics of Deep Space: The team engineered the entire architecture around the constraint of profound signal delay, mandating a 100% offline-capable system (localhost serving, SQLite).
  • Microgravity Adaptation: The team accounted for the fact that fluid shifts and bone density loss are normal in space, which informed the algorithmic decision to base alerts on sudden deviations from a moving baseline rather than rigid Earth standards.
  • Cross-Disciplinary Integration: The team carefully managed the synchronization of diverse technical components, ensuring that complex data payloads from the UI, vision scripts, and language models all routed flawlessly into a unified backend schema without unit mismatches or data loss.
